ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Mother halves the birthday cake. One half she then halves again. Of that she again halves one of the smaller pieces. Of these smaller pieces she once more halves one of them (see diagram). One of the two smallest pieces weighs $100 \mathrm{~g}$.
How much does the entire cake weigh?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached diagram shows a round cake drawn as a cylinder. Several straight cuts meet near the top center area, creating successively smaller wedge-shaped pieces on one side. The smallest visible region is made by the last halving, giving two equal smallest wedge pieces. Reasoning: The text says the whole cake is first halved. Then one of those halves is halved again. Then one of those smaller pieces is halved again. Finally, one of those pieces is halved once more, producing the two smallest equal pieces. So each smallest piece is 1/16 of the whole cake. Since one smallest piece weighs 100 g, the whole cake weighs 100 × 16 = 1600 g. Final answer: 1600 g
